title: The 4D v11 SQL Data File Cache
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Keep Cache in Physical Memory preference

historical_commentary.text: This note documents the 4D v11 SQL cache redesign (3-way associative addressing, larger 32-bit-addressable caches on 64-bit OSes, in-cache BLOB/Picture storage) as a genuine architectural improvement over 4D 2004, and the underlying concepts of purge/flush behavior and cache sizing guidance remain broadly applicable to how the 4D engine manages memory today. However, the specific numeric ceilings discussed (2-4GB caches, 8GB RAM recommendations, 32-bit process limits) are entirely obsolete now that 4D has been a native 64-bit application for years, removing the described 32-bit addressing constraints. GET CACHE STATISTICS and FLUSH BUFFERS remain valid diagnostic commands, so the tooling guidance is still useful even though the hardware-era numbers are historical curiosities.
related_updates: 4D has been a native 64-bit application since v13 (2012), removing the 32-bit cache/address-space ceilings discussed in this note
Modern 4D Server documentation and Runtime Explorer provide updated cache-sizing guidance suited to today's much larger RAM configurations
